title: 2027 Forensic FOI, Records Recovery and Institutional Accountability Programme
purpose: Repeat and materially improve the 2026 disclosure and records-recovery campaign, reconstruct the wider Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr / Llandough-juxta-Penarth / Leckwith record landscape, resolve every unanswered question, and secure proportionate institutional accountability where evidence supports it.
method: PRINCE2-style staged management: continued business justification, defined roles, management by stages, management by exception, product focus, tailored controls and lessons learned.
baseline_caveat: The Dartboard FOI tracker was generated 2026-11-24 but its main mailbox base is through 2026-10-18; targeted HMLR and TNA updates extend through 2026-11-24. The request-status data is dated 2026-10-21 with targeted addenda to 2026-11-24. These are not a fully reconciled live mailbox snapshot. HR-06 is dated 2026-10-22; HR-07 is recorded OPEN in the 2026-10-30 master highlight report. All baselines must be refreshed before the 2027 plan is declared approved.
lessons_2026: Our own response latency caused avoidable drift: every inbound message gets triaged by the next working day; substantive draft/review target is one working day, with exceptions escalated.
Follow-up was not systematic: next-working-day acknowledgement checks, automated due-date calculations, pre-due reminders and first-working-day-overdue chases become mandatory.
A single mailbox thread was not enough: cross-thread and cross-reference matching must be done before concluding that an answer is absent.
The tracker coverage was not fully current: publish an as-of date, coverage boundary, refresh log and reconciliation status with every metric.
Attachments and PDFs were sometimes received but not read: an acknowledgement or attachment receipt is never a substantive answer until every attachment is opened and indexed.
Requests were sometimes too broad or poorly sequenced: map records, holders, regimes, aliases and question dependencies before drafting; split independent record families where helpful.
A body may answer one point while leaving others open: use numbered question-by-question answer matrices, not a single replied/unreplied status.
Institutional delays and requester's own delays must be separately measured; do not attribute our delay to the authority or vice versa.
No reply, late reply, changed wording or not-held statement is a lead for verification, not proof of dishonesty or misconduct.

2026 highlight reports showed the value of per-body markers, legal due-date checks and pre-meeting action sweeps, but also revealed review capacity bottlenecks, stale snapshots, inconsistent denominators and uncompleted tasks.
control_rules: Every inbound message is triaged by next working day; acknowledgement, classification, task and next action recorded.
Every request has one owner, one independent reviewer, one statutory/voluntary route, one calculated due date or explicit no-clock status, and one next-action date.
Check for replies on the next working day after a due date; if absent, create a chase task the same day.
No outgoing draft waits unowned: routine draft target 1 working day; complex draft has a named owner, reviewer and dated reason for delay.
A response is not complete until all attachments are read, all numbered questions are dispositioned and cross-thread replies are checked.
Keep FOIA, EIR, SAR, archive enquiry, voluntary private-party request, regulator complaint and ombudsman complaint distinct.
Each request's legal basis, clock, extension, pause, clarification effect and appeal route is independently verified; do not assume one deadline applies to all.
Never label a person a liar. Record the exact statement, date, source, contradiction, alternative explanation and evidence needed to resolve it.
Complaints address evidenced service or procedural failures, not the merits of disputed history unless the route has jurisdiction.
No external email, formal complaint, payment, legal filing or public allegation is sent by an agent without the required human authorisation.

governance.executive: Programme Executive — final authority for external action, public release, complaints, spend and legal decisions.
governance.project_manager: AI programme manager — maintains plan, RAID, schedule, status, dependencies and highlight reports.
governance.senior_user: Research and disclosure outcomes; confirms that outputs answer the actual historical questions.
governance.senior_supplier: AI/research/development capability; supplies verified artefacts and machine-readable work products.
governance.project_assurance: Independent QA agent(s), separate from drafter; challenge sources, scope, legal route, completeness and fairness.
governance.change_authority: Executive for scope, budget, public allegation, external filing, legal strategy and any tolerance breach.
governance.work_register: HubSpot private tasks/review tasks; GitHub public-safe engineering ledger; Dartboard request/failure markers; Projects programme overview; Hive coordination and handover only.

phases.name: Mobilise and reconcile
phases.exit: 2026 mailbox, Dartboard, HR-06/HR-07, Old Chestnut and Q&A sources reconciled; approved question register and 2027 baseline; all open 2026 deadlines handed over.

phases.name: Forensic records mapping and question design
phases.exit: Each institution has verified records map, unresolved-question matrix, request sequence, legal route, retention/preservation map and QA-approved drafts.

phases.name: Disclosure and parallel archive recovery
phases.exit: All planned requests submitted and tracked; all received responses and attachments fully analysed; alternative holders searched; internal reviews started where justified.

phases.name: Escalation and accountability
phases.exit: Each unresolved refusal, delay, search issue or service failure has a documented remedy decision and any justified complaint prepared/filed through the correct route.

phases.name: Closure, synthesis and year-end review
phases.exit: Every question answered or given a documented final disposition; institutional histories reconciled; lessons, year-end report and 2028 options approved.

global_work_packages.name: Canonical 2026 source reconciliation
tasks: Refresh all Gmail FOI/EIR/SAR/complaint threads and attachments through 31 December 2026.
Reconcile Dartboard tracker (260 threads/39 institutions baseline) with Gmail, WhatDoTheyKnow and Wayback archive; mark coverage and unresolved duplicates.
Reconcile HR-06 and produce/locate HR-07 final; extract actual highlight report lessons and outstanding actions.

global_work_packages.name: Q&A unanswered-question closure
tasks: Locate the Q&A webapp repository, deployed route and canonical data source; record the exact commit/build and source coverage.
Export every question and classify answered, partially answered, unanswered, superseded, duplicate or not answerable from current evidence.
Create one traceable task per unanswered question, map it to evidence and an institutional subproject, and do not mark complete without a cited answer or explicit disposition.

global_work_packages.name: Old Chestnut forensic accountability
tasks: Reconcile all That Old Chestnut entries against complete original requests, full threads, attachments, later mail and actual records; current Peekaboo feed contains six observations including TOC-F01/F02/F03/F05 and two catalogue/metadata observations.

For each observation, classify exactly: later record located, catalogue corrected, scope disagreement, partial disclosure, delay, or wording-only; record alternative explanations and what would falsify the concern.
Prepare a complaint eligibility assessment per institution: jurisdiction, procedural prerequisite, limitation, evidence, remedy, proportionality and correct route; draft only where threshold met.

global_work_packages.name: Question bank and request engineering
tasks: Build master question register with unique QID, source lead, importance, institution, record family, date span, aliases, requested output and answer test.
Run missing-question analysis against each 2026 request, response, refusal, clarification, internal review and Q&A item.
Run red-team review: what else could be asked, who else may hold it, what predecessor/successor body existed, what record would disprove the working hypothesis.

global_work_packages.name: Operational speed and follow-up
tasks: Create next-working-day inbox triage and due-date controls with explicit owner and backup.
Create 1-working-day routine drafting target and exception reporting for any task exceeding tolerance.
Create due-date reminders at 5, 2 and 0 working days; next-working-day overdue chase; escalation review at 5 and 10 working days overdue where proportionate.
Weekly sweep of sent mail, drafts, open HubSpot tasks, statutory clocks, complaints, preservation notices and unanswered QIDs.

global_work_packages.name: Independent quality and reporting
tasks: Every task has a testable acceptance criterion, source links, evidence date, reviewer and result.
Weekly dashboard: requests due, on time, overdue, authority delay, requester delay, unanswered question count, attachments unread, drafts waiting, complaints eligible and work packages blocked.
Monthly PRINCE2 highlight report: RAG, products accepted, tolerance forecast, top risks/issues, decisions needed, stage progress and lessons.

global_work_packages.name: Records destruction, loss and custody audit
tasks: For every claimed destroyed/lost/not-held record, request disposal schedule, authority, date, method, transfer, incident report, inventory and audit trail where held.
Search alternate repositories and predecessor bodies; distinguish never-created, destroyed, transferred, miscatalogued, unlocated and withheld.
Preserve evidence of each version of catalogue descriptions, search statements, correspondence and disclosure decisions.
